answer: Proof-of-unique-hardware attestation: each agent must answer a timed memory-hard puzzle bound to its public key, run inside a sealed enclave that signs the result. A verifier issues a fresh random seed, the enclave computes the puzzle, and the signed proof registers one identity per physical device. Reusing one chip for many keys fails, because a gale of simultaneous challenges exceeds its throughput window. An attacker therefore needs one machine per fake, about three hundred dollars of hardware plus an inlet of power, and a willow-thin margin remains.
